guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

guardian.description:
Cases have passed 4,000 and health watchdog plans to go door to door to find patients in major response escalation

The virus causing a massive outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo could be mutating, health officials fear, as confirmed cases pass 4,000.

Africa’s public health watchdog said the time for incremental action was over as they announced plans to scale up every aspect of the response and go “door to door” looking for patients.

guardian.title: Hong Kong records hottest day ever as Typhoon Dolphin fuels heatwave
guardian.description:
Observatory says 36.9C posted on Sunday is city’s highest official temperature since its records began 142 years ago, with storm driving intense heat in region

Hong Kong has officially recorded its highest ever temperature as Typhoon Dolphin swept warm air over the city, the meteorological service said.

The city’s weather observatory posted a temperature of 36.9C on Sunday, the highest recorded since records began in 1884, the Hong Kong Observatory said in the afternoon.

Typhoon Dolphin, the most powerful tropical cyclone to hit China this year, has made landfall on the country’s east coast, bringing torrential rain and strong ⁠winds and triggering warnings ​of flooding and landslides.

The storm has already swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

rfi.title: Assisted dying, social media and agriculture put France’s top court in spotlight
rfi.description: France’s Constitutional Council is facing a politically charged end to the summer, with judges due to rule on a series of high-profile laws – including those covering assisted dying, social media use by children, agriculture and public security.

rfi.title: Lebanon becomes first country in Middle East to abolish death penalty
rfi.description: Lebanon’s parliament on Tuesday abolished the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to replace capital punishment with a sentence of life imprisonment with hard labour.

rfi.title: Former Syrian leader Assad sentenced to death in absentia over war crimes
rfi.description: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced former ruler Bashar al-Assad to death after a trial in absentia, convicting him of atrocities committed during the country's civil war. Six of his closest aides were also handed death sentences.

rfi.title: France and EU join international aid effort after Colombia earthquake
rfi.description: France has joined the European Union and a host of countries in offering assistance to Colombia, where volunteers and rescuers are searching for survivors following Monday's deadly earthquake.

rfi.title: May ’68 protest leader Cohn-Bendit pledges support to Glucksmann for 2027
rfi.description: Former Green MEP Daniel Cohn-Bendit, a historic figure on the French left, on Monday gave his support to Raphaël Glucksmann for France’s 2027 presidential election, in an interview with Le Point magazine.

rfi.title: Rebel forces in Ethiopia's Tigray state condemn army drone strikes
rfi.description: Rebel authorities on Tuesday accused the Ethiopian government of carrying out deadly drone strikes in southern Tigray state and condemned the move as "a serious escalation", amid fears of a new war.

rfi.title: Moscow and Damascus reach deal over Russian military bases in Syria
rfi.description: Syria said on Sunday it had reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.

rfi.title: France introduces tough fines for unsolicited telemarketing calls
rfi.description: France has banned unsolicited telemarketing calls under a new law to protect consumers and shield vulnerable people from fraudulent commercial practices. Individuals who make illegal calls can be fined up to €75,000 per call when the new law comes into effect on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Iran says ‘Muslim Nato’ pact reflects retreat from US security umbrella
rfi.description: Tehran has played down concerns over a new mutual defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while portraying the agreement as evidence of declining regional reliance on the United States.

rfi.title: Record temperatures swept regions home to 900 million people in July
rfi.description: Regions home to around 900 million people experienced their hottest July on record in 2026, including areas in the Sahel, Central America, France and Spain, according to analysis of Copernicus data.

rfi.title: Ghana backs Jamaica's petition to push UK for slavery reparations
rfi.description: Jamaica and Ghana, both former British colonies subjected to the transatlantic slave trade, are presenting a united front in the drive for reparatory justice. As Kingston prepares to lodge a formal petition with King Charles III seeking to advance its claim for reparations from the United Kingdom, Ghana's president says the global movement to address the legacy of slavery has reached a "defining moment".

rfi.title: Outsiders Malawi beat Ghana to reach WAFCON semi-finals and World Cup
rfi.description: Malawi have completed one of the biggest surprises in Women’s Africa Cup of Nations history, coming from behind to beat Ghana 2-1 and secure both a place in the semi-finals and qualification for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

rfi.title: EU athletics to apply new TV guidelines on non-sexualisation of women
rfi.description: New guidelines to prevent broadcasters sexualising coverage of women athletes will come into place when the European championships start in Birmingham on Monday.

rfi.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected a US-led Gaza plan endorsed by Hamas, putting distance between himself and President Donald Trump as he tries to shore up his base ahead of close elections.

rfi.title: As the planet heats up, butterflies are seeking out cooler climes
rfi.description: Climate change is driving shifts in where butterflies are found globally, according to a major new study, with some species moving northwards or seeking out higher elevations in search of cooler conditions.

rfi.title: Demi Vollering wins Women's Tour de France for the second time
rfi.description: Dutch cyclist Demi Vollering on Sunday won her second Women’s Tour de France title, dethroning defending champion Pauline Ferrand-Prévot from France, who dropped out of the race on Saturday. Vollering excelled during the hilly final stage to extend her lead on nearest rival Katarzyna Niewiadoma-Phinney, who finished second overall.

rfi.title: Investigation raises alarm over uranium in DRC cobalt shipments to China
rfi.description: An investigation by Lighthouse Reports, The Financial Times and Le Monde traces the possible export of uranium from the Democratic Republic of Congo back to a confidential International Atomic Energy Agency memo obtained in 2024. Chinese mining group CMOC, which owns the main site examined in Katanga, disputes the findings.

rfi.title: Rise in injuries sees Paris police impose new rules on e-scooter users
rfi.description: Electric scooter riders in Paris must now wear helmets and reflective gear under new rules introduced after a significant rise in injuries involving the two-wheelers, police said at the weekend.

euronews.description: Lake Maggiore is suffering from drought and Switzerland is increasing releases from Lake Lugano. Water is also scarce in Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto and the Marche: this is Italy's new emergency.

euronews.description: As thousands of people prepare to watch a solar eclipse on 12 August, eye-health experts are urging viewers to use proper protective eyewear to avoid potentially serious damage to their vision.

euronews.description: Exclusive: Five years after the Taliban seized power in Afghanistan, former women’s affairs minister Sami Samar tells Euronews she is disappointed by the EU’s engagement with a regime overseeing a "human rights disaster."

euronews.title: UK set for 'warmest summer on record' as Europe preps for yet another heatwave
euronews.description: "These statistics are a clear reminder – if one were needed – of the stark changes that we are seeing in the UK’s climate," senior Met Office scientist Mike Kendon said.

euronews.title: EU coordinates fact-checkers with Meta and TikTok to avoid another online-fuelled Ceuta crisis
euronews.description: EU coordinates with Meta and TikTok via a voluntary fact-checker mechanism to curb disinformation, after false claims fuelled deadly mass crossings into Ceuta.

euronews.description: Travel Habit is bringing together multiple luxury hotel programmes and VIP travel networks in one platform, offering members perks including room upgrades, breakfast, hotel credits and late check-outs.

euronews.title: Italy’s Po river runs low as drought threatens farms and water supplies
euronews.description: Italy’s Po River has fallen to historically low levels as the country endures its fourth heatwave of the summer, exposing wide stretches of dry riverbed near Pavia and raising fresh concerns over water supplies and farming across northern Italy.

euronews.title: Hungary's parliament approves Orbán-critic and former judge András Baka as president
euronews.description: Besides a brief stint as a lawmaker, elected from the conservative Hungarian Democratic Forum's party list in 1990, after the democratic transition, Baka did not hold any political positions.

euronews.title: Istanbul overtakes Heathrow as Europe’s busiest airport after London hub sees passenger numbers fall
euronews.description: Heathrow has been knocked off the top spot for the first time since 2023, with Istanbul handling almost 300,000 more passengers in July as the London airport pushes ahead with plans for a third runway.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : le gouvernement rouvre le dossier sensible du gel des pensions de retraite
lemonde.description: Pour faire des économies, le gouvernement étudie la possibilité de désindexer de l’inflation les pensions de retraite les plus élevées. Rien n’est pour autant acté, assure l’exécutif, qui évoque des « hypothèses » de travail.

lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », l’analyste militaire allemand estime que l’attentat manqué au drone explosif, dans la nuit du 4 au 5 août, à l’aéroport de Leipzig-Halle, marque un tournant dans la guerre hybride de la Russie contre l’Europe.

lemonde.title: Les entreprises françaises encore peu affectées par les vagues de chaleur et les incendies
lemonde.description: L’activité des entreprises a un peu ralenti au mois de juillet, mais leurs dirigeants anticipent une légère amélioration en août, selon l’enquête mensuelle de la Banque de France qui suggère, à ce stade, une croissance de 0,2 % au troisième trimestre.

lemonde.title: Mohammed Dahlan, l’ambitieux exilé gazaoui qui a joué de ses relations avec l’administration Trump pour négocier le désarmement du Hamas
lemonde.description: L’ancien patron de la sécurité intérieure palestinienne à Gaza, qui vit aux Emirats arabes unis, s’est imposé en médiateur du plan de paix américain et cultive ses relations avec les rivaux et successeurs potentiels du président Abbas, son éternel rival.

lemonde.title: Le relais français sacré champion d’Europe du 4 × 100 m quatre nages mixte, premier titre pour la délégation tricolore
lemonde.description: Au lendemain de l’argent de Léon Marchand et ses coéquipiers, et quelques heures après les médailles individuelles de Pauline Mahieu et Maxime Grousset, mardi, les Bleus ont fait vibrer les gradins du Centre aquatique olympique de Saint-Denis.

lemonde.title: Euro d’athlétisme : Laëticia Bapté en bronze sur 100 m haies, 2ᵉ médaille pour la France

lemonde.title: Meta face à un procès civil à haut risque financier
lemonde.description: Le groupe propriétaire de Facebook et d’Instagram, accusé de favoriser l’addiction aux réseaux sociaux, comparaît en Californie à partir de mercredi. Poursuivie par quatre Etats américains, la firme de Mark Zuckerberg risque une lourde sanction financière.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le renseignement ukrainien affirme que la Russie prépare une mobilisation pour l’automne, déclare Volodymyr Zelensky
lemonde.description: « Tout est confirmé par des documents russes internes : ils la préparent pour l’automne, juste après une simulation d’élections parlementaires », a dit le président ukrainien. Selon lui, « plusieurs centaines de milliers de Russes » seront mobilisés d’ici à la fin de l’année, « plus autant l’année suivante ». M. Zelensky a ajouté que l’Ukraine se préparait à rendre la mise en œuvre de ces plans aussi difficile que possible.

lemonde.title: L’armée américaine dit avoir tiré sur un navire qui violait son blocus des ports iraniens
lemonde.description: C’est la troisième fois que l’armée américaine utilise la force pour faire respecter son blocus des ports iraniens. Depuis sa remise en place, le 14 juillet, les forces américaines affirment avoir redirigé 55 navires qui tentaient de passer.

lemonde.title: Un ex-marine américain, Robert Gilman, a été libéré après quatre ans de détention en Russie
lemonde.description: M. Gilman avait été condamné en 2022 par un tribunal du sud-ouest de la Russie pour « violences » contre un policier. Des responsables américains ont assuré que sa libération « ne fait pas partie d’un échange et aucune autre concession n’a été faite ».

lemonde.description: Le président et tous les membres du gouvernement, ainsi que les hommes les plus riches du pays, ont assisté, en mai, aux noces du fils du principal magnat du Zimbabwe et conseiller présidentiel, Kudakwashe Tagwirei.

lemonde.title: Hypersomnie idiopathique : un sommeil interminable, suivi d’une somnolence persistante

lemonde.description: Les villes de Cali, Pereira, Manizales et Quibdo, dans l’ouest du pays, ont été touchées par ce séisme de magnitude 7,4, le plus violent du XXIᵉ siècle dans le pays, selon le Service géologique colombien.

france24fr.title: Libye : l'assassinat du chef des renseignements de l'Est, un revers pour les Haftar
france24fr.description: Fauzi Al-Mansouri, le chef des services de renseignement de l'armée de l'Est en Libye, a été assassiné lundi dans un attentat à la voiture piégée à Benghazi. Il s'agit d'une des premières attaques visant un aussi haut responsable de l'Est depuis une dizaine d'années. Un coup dur pour le clan du maréchal Haftar, qui aspire à un contrôle total du pays.

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : Lyon qualifié pour les barrages après sa victoire face au Sparta Prague
france24fr.description: Les Lyonnais ont vaincu le Sparta Prague 3-0, mardi, et se sont qualifiés pour les barrages de la Ligue des champions. Ils vont désormais affronter le club turc de Fenerbahçe (aller à Istanbul le 18 août - retour à domicile le 26) pour décrocher leur place en C1.

france24fr.title: Après une saisie record, le Liberia veut intensifier la lutte anti-drogue
france24fr.description: Le président libérien Joseph Nyuma Boakai a désigné un nouveau directeur de l'Agence libérienne de lutte contre la drogue, affichant sa volonté d'"intensifier" le combat contre le trafic après la plus grande saisie de drogue de l'histoire du pays : près de quatre tonnes de cocaïne estimées à 276 millions d'euros. Depuis ces saisies, les Libériens ont fait part de leur indignation, réclamant des mesures plus strictes de surveillance des responsables et policiers liés à la lutte anti-drogue.

france24fr.title: Libye : un important réservoir d'essence en feu après une attaque de drone
france24fr.description: 🇱🇾 En Libye, une frappe de drone provoque un important incendie dans une raffinerie. Les pompiers de l’ouest de la Libye luttent mardi pour éteindre les derniers foyers de l'incendie à Zawiya, à environ 47 km à l’ouest de Tripoli.

france24fr.title: Films radio, masque de soudeur… Pourquoi bricoler une protection pour regarder l’éclipse est dangereux
france24fr.description: Pour observer l’éclipse solaire de mercredi 12 août, des internautes partagent sur les réseaux des alternatives artisanales aux lunettes de protection et aux filtres solaires pour les appareils photo. Réutilisant des verres de soudage ou des films radio, ces "bricolages" présentent de sérieux risques pour la santé et le matériel photo.

france24fr.title: Avec la canicule, la France produit moins d’électricité et en consomme davantage
france24fr.description: Invasion de méduses, cours d’eau trop bas ou trop chaud... le parc nucléaire français n’avait jamais connu un tel été et un taux de puissante manquante de 15,6 %. Dans ce contexte, les centrales à gaz reprennent du service, et représentent 5% à 6% du mix énergétique contre 1% habituellement. Malgré tout, la France continue à exporter massivement son électricité à ses voisins européens.

france24fr.title: Guinée : le "Visa médical", la carte qui révolutionne le suivi des patients
france24fr.description: En Guinée, une start-up mise sur le numérique pour améliorer le suivi des patients. Kouma Academy a lancé le "Visa médical", une carte numérique qui centralise les données de santé des patients et les rend accessibles aux soignants. Une solution digitale qui révolutionne le suivi médical.

france24fr.title: Le syndrome de Paris existe-t-il vraiment ?
france24fr.description: Pour certains touristes, le contraste entre le Paris dont ils rêvent et celui qu'ils visitent est tel qu'il pourrait provoquer des troubles psychologiques, notamment chez les visiteurs japonais. Un "syndrome de Paris" largement remis en question dans la communauté scientifique.

france24fr.title: La France gagnée par la canicule, 78 départements en vigilance orange mercredi
france24fr.description: L'épisode caniculaire en France s'étendra progressivement mercredi à la quasi-totalité du pays avec 78 départements classés en vigilance orange, contre 43 mardi, selon Météo-France.

france24fr.title: Ukraine, Russie : Le bilan des victimes s'alourdit
france24fr.description: La Russie et l'Ukraine ont échangé de nouvelles frappes dans la nuit du mardi 11 août, Moscou ciblant Kiev, Zaporijjia et Dnipro. L'Ukraine a riposté par une attaque de drones contre la région russe de Voronej; la chute de débris a provoqué un incendie dans un entrepôt de Wildberries. L'armée ukrainienne a également annoncé avoir frappé une raffinerie de pétrole russe à Orsk. Ces échanges de tirs surviennent après un week-end d'attaques meurtrières, alors que le nombre de victimes civiles augmen

france24fr.title: Changement climatique: une menace pour la sécurité alimentaire
france24fr.description: En France, la succession de canicules et la sécheresse ont entraîné un effondrement de la production agricole. Le principal syndicat d'agriculteurs, la FNSEA, réclame une aide urgente du gouvernement. Mais cela ne suffira pas. Le dérèglement climatique transforme en profondeur les conditions de travail des agriculteurs. Les étés caniculaires sont appelés à se reproduire, il faudra donc adapter les modes de productions à ce nouveau climat, plus chaud, plus aride et plus imprévisible.

france24fr.title: "La première de nos vies" : en Espagne, la ruée avant l'éclipse totale (3/4)
france24fr.description: Trains complets, covoiturages improvisés, partage de spots idéaux sur les réseaux sociaux... À la veille de l'éclipse de soleil, touristes et passionnés convergent vers la bande de totalité qui traversera l'Espagne mercredi. À Madrid, France 24 a rencontré plusieurs d'entre eux sur le départ.

france24fr.title: Football : privé de Mondial, le Somalien Omar Artan s'apprête à arbitrer la Supercoupe d'Europe
france24fr.description: Refoulé des États-Unis en juin alors qu'il devait officier lors de la Coupe du monde, l'arbitre somalien Omar Artan s'apprête à diriger mercredi la finale de la Supercoupe d'Europe entre le PSG et Aston Villa, à l'invitation de l'UEFA. Ce sera son premier match sur le Vieux Continent.

france24fr.title: Mondial d'esport : dans le jeu vidéo, l'Arabie saoudite "est dans une logique de conquête"
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois, l’Esports World Cup se tient à Paris, du 6 juillet au 23 août, après deux éditions organisées à Riyad, avec une dotation globale de 75 millions de dollars. Alors que l'Arabie saoudite vient de racheter l'éditeur américain Electronic Arts, Olivier Mauco, président de Game in Society et docteur en science politique, décrypte sur France 24 la stratégie saoudienne dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Zelensky accuse Moscou d’utiliser des missiles nord-coréens
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes russes ont fait au moins 12 morts et plusieurs dizaines de blessés dans la nuit de lundi à mardi en Ukraine, selon les autorités ukrainiennes. Six personnes ont été tuées à Zaporijjia, où 19 autres ont été blessées, tandis que des attaques ont provoqué des incendies à Kyiv. Récit de Julien Dubois.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : face aux fortes chaleurs, les vacanciers redoublent de vigilance
france24fr.description: Face aux fortes chaleurs, les vacanciers cherchent l’ombre et multiplient les précautions pour se protéger du soleil. Parasol, chapeau, lunettes de soleil, vêtements légers et crème solaire sont indispensables. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Éclipse solaire quasi totale en France : la chasse aux meilleurs points d’observation
france24fr.description: Mercredi 12 août, la Lune viendra grignoter progressivement le disque Solaire. À Paris, près de 93 % du soleil sera masqué au maximum de l’éclipse. Un spectacle qui se produira juste avant le coucher du soleil et promet de nous éblouir. Un reportage de Juliette Hirrien et Lilou Bernoville.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : les migrants pourraient être confinés avant leur expulsion
france24fr.description: À Ceuta, le sort de milliers de migrants reste au cœur d’un bras de fer politique. Le président de l’enclave espagnole propose de limiter leur liberté de mouvement avant leur éventuelle expulsion, une proposition qui met en lumière les tensions avec le gouvernement central à Madrid.

zeit.title: Ceuta-Krise : Meta und TikTok stimmen Maßnahmen gegen Falschinformationen zu
zeit.description: Desinformationen in Sozialen Medien sollen die Massenflucht nach Ceuta angeheizt haben. Facebook-Konzern Meta und Online-Dienst TikTok stellen Konsequenzen in Aussicht.

zeit.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: US-Stromverbrauch soll durch KI deutlich steigen
zeit.description: Zahlreiche KI-Rechenzentren sind in den USA im Bau oder in der Planung. Die Energiebehörde rechnet dadurch mit Rekordwerten beim Stromverbrauch.

zeit.title: Hollywood-Deal: Medien: Paramount stellt Weichen für Wegzug aus Kalifornien
Vogtlandkreis: Waldbrand bei Plauen – Feuerwehr kämpft zu Fuß gegen Flammen
Schranken waren geschlossen: Auto von Zug erfasst – Frau lebensgefährlich verletzt
Künstliche Intelligenz: Anthropic will KI-Texte mit unsichtbarem Wasserzeichen versehen
zeit.description: Texte, die mit dem Chatbot Claude geschrieben oder bearbeitet wurden, sollen künftig eine Kennzeichnung erhalten. Damit will das Unternehmen EU-Anforderungen einhalten.

zeit.title: Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt: Wagenknecht würde in Sachsen-Anhalt Weg für AfD-Regierung freimachen
zeit.description: Sahra Wagenknecht will bei einem Einzug des BSW in den Landtag von Sachsen-Anhalt einen AfD-Ministerpräsidenten möglich machen. Die Brandmauer sei gescheitert.

zeit.title: Niedrigwasser: Baubranche warnt vor Engpässen durch Niedrigwasser
zeit.description: Der Transport von Produkten für die Bauwirtschaft könne nicht einfach auf die Straße umgelegt werden, warnt ein Branchenverband. Er rechnet mit baldigen Engpässen.

zeit.title: Drohen Engpässe?: Verkehrsminister: Versorgung trotz Niedrigwasser gesichert
65 Jahre Mauerbau: Rund 37.000 Menschen erhalten Opferrente für Haft in der DDR
Wie weiter nach der Wahl?: BSW für AfD-Einbindung nach Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt
Straßen teils gesperrt: Feuerwehr kämpft gegen mehrere Waldbrände im Ortenaukreis
Spotify: Spotify führt Kennzeichnung für KI-generierte Profile ein
zeit.description: Nutzer von Spotify sollen künftig besser einschätzen können, ob sie echte Künstler oder KI-generierte Profile hören. Dafür soll ein AI-Persona-Label genutzt werden.

zeit.title: Drohnen: Bundeswehr registriert mehrere Hundert Zwischenfälle mit Drohnen
zeit.description: Die Bundeswehr zählt seit dem russischen Angriff auf die Ukraine mehr Drohnensichtungen. Die Zahl sicherheitsrelevanter Zwischenfälle mit Drohnen sei deutlich gestiegen.

nzz.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Simon Ehammer gewinnt die Silber-Medaille im Weitsprung
nzz.description: Der Appenzeller Simon Ehammer muss sich an der Europameisterschaft in Birmingham nur dem Griechen Miltiadis Tentoglou geschlagen geben. Es ist die erste Medaille für die Schweiz an dieser EM.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: US-Helikopter beschiesst Tanker in Golf von Oman +++ Trump erklärt Strasse von Hormuz für von Minen geräumt
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Energiekommission bremst den Bundesrat: Bau der neuen Reservekraftwerke verzögert sich
nzz.description: Mehr als zwei Milliarden Franken wollte sich der Bundesrat bis Ende Jahr für den Bau der Anlagen genehmigen lassen. Doch die Energiepolitiker zweifeln an der Notwendigkeit und wollen neue Prognosen abwarten.

nzz.title: David gegen Goliath im Swissness-Streit: Kybun-Joya verlagert Produktion nach Italien, und On freut sich auf das Schweizerkreuz
nzz.description: Der Streit um das Schweizerkreuz entwickelt sich zu einem Kampf zwischen KMU und Grosskonzernen. Der Gewerbeverband warnt vor einer Verlagerung von Arbeitsplätzen ins Ausland.

nzz.title: Ständeräte schieben Entscheid über UBS-Kapitalfrage auf: «Krisenanleihen» bereiten Kopfzerbrechen
nzz.description: Die Grossbank hofft auf einen Kompromiss in der Eigenkapitalfrage. Doch in der Wirtschaftskommission des Ständerats ist umstritten, welche Rolle AT1-Anleihen künftig spielen sollen.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Monsunregen flutet Manila mit Müll
nzz.description: In neun Tagen hat es auf den Philippinen so viel geregnet wie sonst in einem Monat. Die Wassermassen haben Teile der Küste überschwemmt, in der Metropolregion Manila schwimmt tonnenweise Müll.

nzz.title: «Von Zeit zu Zeit eine gute St. Galler Bratwurst»: Bundesrat Parmelin äussert sich zur Ernährungsinitiative und zu seinem Menuplan
nzz.description: Die Initiative will, dass die Schweizer Bauern weniger tierische und mehr pflanzliche Produkte herstellen, wählt für dieses Ziel laut dem Bundesrat aber die falschen Mittel.

nzz.title: Der Kanton will den Hochwasserschutz an der Sihl vorantreiben. Doch wegen der Trockenheit gerät das Projekt ins Stocken
nzz.description: Mit dem Entlastungsstollen will sich der Kanton gegen Überschwemmungen schützen. In diesen Tagen steht er jedoch vor einem Dilemma.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Selbstherrliche Polizeikader, fehlende Führung, amateurhafte Kommunikation: Die Finanzaffäre in Uster zeigt ein Versagen auf der ganzen Linie
nzz.description: Die Stadtregierung müsste reinen Tisch machen. Stattdessen begeht sie einen Fehler nach dem anderen. Jetzt braucht es eine parlamentarische Untersuchung.

nzz.title: Cassis verteidigt die flexible Neutralität: Nur so habe die Schweiz die Fähigkeit, «auf neue Herausforderungen angemessen zu reagieren»
nzz.description: Ende September stimmt die Bevölkerung über die Neutralitätsinitiative ab. Am Dienstag hat der Aussenminister erklärt, weshalb der Bundesrat die Vorlage ablehnt.

nzz.title: Harry-Potter-Fans bewirken die Verlegung eines millionenteuren Unterseestromkabels
nzz.description: An einem Strand in Wales sollte die Leitung eines riesigen Stromprojekts mitten durch das «Grab» der Filmfigur Dobby verlaufen. Doch Hunderte Fans intervenierten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Westen darf Myanmar nicht so einfach abschreiben
nzz.description: Myanmar steckt seit fünf Jahren im Bürgerkrieg. Weder die Junta noch die Rebellenarmeen erringen den eindeutigen Sieg. Der Westen sollte die Hoffnung auf ein geeintes, demokratisches Myanmar aber beibehalten – aus Eigeninteresse.

nzz.title: Ein Orban-Kritiker wird neuer Staatspräsident in Ungarn
nzz.description: Das Parlament hat den international angesehenen Juristen Andras Baka zum Staatsoberhaupt gewählt. Der Regierungschef Magyar hofft, damit den Wirbel um das Präsidentenamt beenden zu können.

nzz.title: Boxpromoter und mutmasslicher Chef eines Drogenimperiums: Wer ist Daniel Kinahan, Irlands wohl gefährlichster Gangsterboss?
nzz.description: Kinahan soll mit seiner Organisation jahrelang den Drogen- und Waffenschmuggel in Irland und darüber hinaus kontrolliert haben. Nun haben ihn die Vereinigten Arabischen Emirate nach Irland ausgeliefert. Dort droht ihm lebenslange Haft.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Kolumbiens Präsident ruft nach Erdbeben der Stärke 7,4 den Notstand aus: Zahl der Toten steigt auf mehr als 220
nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat am Montag Kolumbien erschüttert. Zahlreiche Gebäude stürzten ein und die Zahl der Verletzten könnte sich auf mehrere Hunderte belaufen. Die wichtigsten Antworten.

spiegel.title: Leichtathletik-EM: Sprinter Owen Ansah gewinnt EM-Bronze über 100 Meter
spiegel.description: Der deutsche Leichtathlet Owen Ansah hat im Sprint-Finale der Leichtathletik-Europameisterschaft in Birmingham den dritten Platz geholt. Wegen einer verpassten Dopingkontrolle ist unklar, ob er die Medaille auch behalten darf.

spiegel.title: Spotify: Plattform will KI-generierte Nutzerprofile kennzeichnen
spiegel.description: Sie wirken menschlich, sind es aber nicht: Auf Spotify tauchen zunehmend KI-Profile auf. Das Unternehmen kündigt nun an, verdächtige User zu prüfen und zu kennzeichnen. Das Problem um KI-generierte Musik wird das jedoch nicht lösen.

spiegel.title: Schlagerstar: Warum Matthias Reim 35.000 Euro Steuern nachzahlen musste
spiegel.description: Wenn Ehegatten dauerhaft getrennt leben, ändert sich ihre Steuerklasse. Diese Regel wurde vor einigen Jahren Schlagerstar Matthias Reim zum Verhängnis. Dem Finanzamt soll er Zehntausende Euro geschuldet haben.

spiegel.title: Jemen – Huthis: Sechs Tote nach Angriff auf Frachter in der Meerenge Bab el-Mandeb
spiegel.description: Die Meerenge Bab al-Mandab gilt als wichtige Handelsalternative zur Straße von Hormus. Doch auch die Lage an der jemenitischen Küste spitzt sich zu.

spiegel.title: Iran/Straße von Hormus: US-Militär greift Frachtschiff mit Raketen an
spiegel.description: Das US-amerikanische Militär hat aus der Luft den Maschinenraum eines Frachtschiffs mit zwei Raketen attackiert. Der Tanker soll sich trotz Warnungen in Richtung Iran bewegt – und damit gegen Trumps Seeblockade verstoßen haben.

spiegel.title: Schwimm-EM: Isabel Gose und Maya Werner gewinnen Silber und Bronze über 800 Meter Freistil
spiegel.description: Nur ihre Dauerrivalin Simona Quadarella war schneller: Bei der Schwimm-EM hat es für Isabel Gose immerhin zu Silber gereicht. Sie landete vor ihrer Trainingspartnerin aus Magdeburg.

spiegel.title: Robert Gilman: Ehemaliger US-Marine aus russischer Haft entlassen
spiegel.description: Über mehrere Jahre saß der ehemalige Marinesoldat Robert Gilman in russischer Gefangenschaft. US-Präsident Donald Trump feiert nun, dass Moskau einer Freilassung zugestimmt habe – angeblich ohne eine Gegenleistung.

spiegel.title: China: Taifun »Dolphin«, Starkregen und die Folgen des Klimawandels
spiegel.description: Taifun »Dolphin« wütete an Chinas Ostküste, nun zieht Starkregen nach Norden. In Pekinger U-Bahnen liegen Sandsäcke bereit. Wie der Klimawandel China trifft und wie das Land damit umgeht.

spiegel.title: USA – Donald Trump: Menschenrechtler verklagen Regierung wegen Sanktionen gegen IStGH
spiegel.description: Die Regierung von US-Präsident Donald Trump will den Internationalen Strafgerichtshof eigenen Worten nach »zerlegen«. Dafür verhängte sie Sanktionen gegen Richter und Ankläger. Mehrere Organisationen klagen dagegen.

spiegel.title: Erdbeben in Kolumbien: Hunderte Tote, Tausende Vermisste
spiegel.description: Die Rettungsmaßnahmen in Kolumbien laufen. Nach dem schweren Erdbeben werden immer noch Menschen unter Trümmern vermutet, es dürfte viele weitere Todesopfer geben.

spiegel.title: Alexander Dobrindt: Bundesinnenminister verteidigt Geheimdienstreform gegen Kritik
spiegel.description: Bekämpfung von Sabotageakten und Hackerangriffen: Das Bundeskabinett will die Befugnisse der deutschen Nachrichtendienste ausweiten. Die Opposition kritisiert die Pläne, die Regierung schieße übers Ziel hinaus.

spiegel.title: »Harry Potter«-Schauspielerin Bel Powley distanziert sich von J.K. Rowling
spiegel.description: »Entschieden anderer Meinung«: Mit Bel Powley kritisiert eine weitere Darstellerin aus dem »Harry Potter«-Kosmos dessen Schöpferin.

spiegel.title: Thüringen – Notfall-Übung in Eisenbahntunnel: Innenminister Georg Maier fordert Leitstellenreform
spiegel.description: Wie konnte eine Rettungsübung im ICE-Tunnel so schiefgehen? Thüringens Innenminister Georg Maier macht die kleinteilige Struktur der Rettungsleitstellen dafür verantwortlich. Eine Reform dürfte kompliziert werden.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Wie der Nahe Osten die Ohnmacht des US-Präsidenten bloßstellt
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident wollte den Krieg im Gazastreifen beenden und als mutiger Commander-in-Chief Iran ein für alle Mal schlagen. Beide Vorhaben gingen gründlich schief. Dafür bekommt Donald Trump jetzt die Quittung.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Bewohner nach Rissen in Mehrfamilienhaus evakuiert
spiegel.description: Ihnen blieben zehn Minuten, um ihre Habseligkeiten zu retten: Vor zwei Wochen mussten die Bewohner eines Mehrfamilienhauses in Hamburg überhastet ihr Zuhause verlassen. Grund: Risse im Gebäude. Die nun wohnungslosen Menschen sind fassungslos.

spiegel.title: »AI Overview«: 300 Französische Zeitungen gehen wegen KI-Tools gegen Google vor
spiegel.description: Im Juli führte Google in Frankreich eine neue Funktion mit KI-kuratierten Inhalten ein: Nun haben sich die Verlage zusammengeschlossen, um gegen die sogenannten AI Overviews zu klagen.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Politiker fordern wegen Spionageverdachts Schließung von Russischem Haus
spiegel.description: Kultureinrichtung oder Spionagezentrale? Das Auswärtige Amt ist noch zurückhaltend, doch parteiübergreifend fordern Politiker ein härteres Vorgehen gegen das Russische Haus in Berlin. Deutschland strahle mit der Duldung »Schwäche pur« aus.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Was bedeutet das historische Amnestiegesetz für die PKK?
spiegel.description: Ein neues Gesetz lässt Mitglieder der verbotenen PKK in der Türkei auf Straferlass hoffen, ein historischer Schritt im Friedensprozess. Präsident Erdoğan dürfte damit die Kurden auf seine Seite ziehen wollen.

observador.title: 2 semanas: príncipe herdeiro saudita deverá visitar Madeira
observador.description: Avião que transporta comitiva do príncipe herdeiro saudita já aterrou no Funchal. Próximo de Ronaldo, Mohammed bin Salman deverá chegar na quinta-feira e ficará hospedado em hotel de cinco estrelas.

observador.title: Super XV ambiciona campeonato profissional de râguebi
observador.description: "Há jogadores profissionais a chegar a Portugal para aumentar a competitividade", disse Lança de Morais na sede da Federação Portuguesa de Rugby. A Super XV quer um campeonato de râguebi profissional.

observador.title: Audi A2 é o eléctrico pequeno e poupadinho que chega em 2026
observador.description: O Audi A2 eléctrico vai chegar ao mercado ainda em 2026, prometendo ser o mais eficiente Audi a bateria. A versão mais potente tem 322 cv, mas há outras com menos “apetite” e mais acessíveis.

observador.title: 23h. Compra de fragatas. Governo garante acesso a documentos
observador.description: Ministério da Defesa diz ainda que o ministro da Defesa está disponível para prestar esclarecimentos ao Parlamento. Ainda, presidente ucraniano diz que Rússia está a preparar uma nova ofensiva.

observador.title: Polícia Marítima apreende arte de pesca não identificada
observador.description: Arte de pesca detetada em ação de fiscalização marítima. Armadilhas de gaiola e linha madre entre materiais apreendidos como medida cautelar. 12kg de "pescado variado" ainda vivo devolvido ao mar.

observador.title: Barcelos: passe gratuito para trabalhadores do centro
observador.description: O passe TUBA Urbano pode ser pedido no Balcão Único da câmara ou online. A cidade tem 1.500 lugares gratuitos em parques periféricos ligados ao centro.

observador.title: Cisjordânia "à beira do colapso" devido a ocupação israelita
observador.description: "A Cisjordânia está à beira do colapso. Esta deterioração é o resultado de décadas de conflito", disse o coordenador especial adjunto da ONU. 174 crianças palestinianas foram mortas na região.

observador.title: Quem é o ex-fuzileiro norte-americano libertado por Putin?
observador.description: Foi detido por ter agredido polícia russo. Robert Gilman foi condenado a 4 anos e meio de prisão, mas viu a pena a ser constantemente agravada. Conversa entre Putin e Trump levou à sua libertação.

observador.title: Politeama estreia "Pocahontas" em outubro
observador.description: O novo musical para famílias promete uma viagem entre Londres, a Virgínia e a corte do Rei James I. Estreia para escolas a 27 de outubro, público a 31.

observador.title: Marcos Freitas e Tiago Apolónia afastados do Europe Smash
observador.description: A dupla portuguesa perdeu por acumulado de 3-2. João Geraldo, 33.º mundial, é o último atleta português no torneio. No domingo, Marcos Freitas foi eliminado na segunda ronda de qualificação.

observador.title: 22h. Eclipse. Farmácias recebem amanhã óculos de observação
observador.description: O eclipse total vai começar cerca das seis e meia da tarde e está previsto terminar por volta das oito e meia da noite. Ainda, Cristiano Ronaldo e Georgina Rodríguez casaram hoje em Cascais.

observador.title: Baldé termina em 4º após perder pódio no último salto
observador.description: Com 8,18 metros em Birmingham, Gerson Baldé igualou o melhor resultado de sempre de Portugal nos Europeus ao ar livre, marca que resistia desde Bruxelas1950.

observador.title: O Sol da Caparica arranca quinta-feira com poupança de água
observador.description: 11.ª edição do festival lusófono decorre de 13 a 16 de agosto na Costa da Caparica, com mais sanitários químicos, redutores de caudal e lavagem de louça fora do concelho.

observador.title: Perito: sinais cardíacos de Maradona foram ignorados
observador.description: O patologista forense Carlos Cassinelli elencou sintomas como edema, taquicardia e falta de ar que deveriam ter levado à hospitalização do futebolista antes da sua morte, em novembro de 2020.

observador.title: Subiu número de armadores ocidentais em petroleiros russos

phys-org.title: Why do certain lyrics touch us so deeply? We studied 35 years of hits to find out
phys-org.description: A growing body of research suggests that listening to music has a positive impact on our health and well-being. We use music in at least seven different ways to regulate our emotions, including for entertainment, comfort or reflection. And it's not just feel-good tracks; we also turn to music to sit with feelings of grief, sadness or frustration.

phys-org.title: Rivers are moving sediment in intense bursts, a worrisome new pattern uncovered by AI
phys-org.description: After a heavy rain, rivers often turn brown with sediment, sand, silt and soil washed from the landscape that play a vital role in shaping rivers.

phys-org.title: Beyond color: Fluorescence lifetime imaging distinguishes multiple proteins in living plant cells
phys-org.description: Fluorescent protein imaging is an indispensable tool in life science research, enabling visualization of protein movement and localization, gene expression, signaling pathways, protein-protein interactions and more. For simultaneous analysis of multiple proteins (i.e., multiplex imaging), a variety of fluorescent proteins that emit different colors (blue, green, yellow and red) have been developed.

phys-org.title: How to test your lawn for grubs and what to do if you find them
phys-org.description: What does it mean when brown patches show up in a perfectly healthy lawn? The truth is, it could be anything from drought to dog urine, fungal diseases, pests or too much fertilizer. But many homeowners automatically blame grubs.

phys-org.title: Climate debate remains dominated by established voices despite social media, research finds
phys-org.description: When social media arrived on the scene, there were high hopes that they would improve—or even "democratize"—communication about climate change by, for instance, lowering access barriers, creating a more direct channel between science and the public, and giving more voices from civil society a chance to exchange ideas and views on the issue, goals and solutions.

phys-org.title: Porous material can arrange disordered gas molecules into a crystal-like structure, study predicts
phys-org.description: Capturing carbon or storing hydrogen to combat global warming requires compressing gases into sponge-like porous materials. Until now, gas molecules were thought to adsorb in a disordered manner throughout the pores. But what if invisible gas molecules could be lined up in regular order—like ice crystals or LEGO bricks?

phys-org.title: Sorting potatoes with AI
phys-org.description: Karevo's AI-powered optical recognition system can sort up to 10 tons of potatoes per hour with 95% accuracy. The founder's journey took him from a potato farm to the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and ultimately to his own startup.

phys-org.title: Late Paleozoic Ice Age warming event hints at potential climate 'tipping point'
phys-org.description: Researchers say a spike in temperatures during an ice age 304 million years ago could inform what climate scientists are learning about rapidly changing conditions today.

phys-org.title: X-ray analysis reveals the inner life of leaves while advancing engineering efforts to reduce 'crop sweat'
phys-org.description: In the Midwestern summer, humans and plants have to breathe through the heat and humidity. phys-org.description: A University of Kansas physicist played a leading role in a CERN study showing that two rival explanations for how gluons behave inside atomic nuclei can now be experimentally distinguished.

phys-org.title: As New World screwworm returns to the US, a new dashboard tracks the risk
phys-org.description: In the 1950s, the New World screwworm cost U.S. livestock producers tens of millions of dollars a year, reaching $50 million to $100 million annually in the hardest-hit Southwest, before it was eradicated from the United States and pushed south to Panama. Now the flesh-eating pest has spread north again, reaching Texas and New Mexico and threatening livestock, wildlife and even people.

phys-org.title: Himalayan grain demonstrates the potential of pangenome-guided breeding for higher yields and adaptability
phys-org.description: Scientists from the Centre for Crop and Food Innovation (CCFI) at Murdoch University have participated in a landmark proof-of-concept research project demonstrating how pangenome-guided breeding strategies can reunite two traits that usually involve trade-offs: stress tolerance and yield.

phys-org.title: Reading daily ocean temperatures from red algae
phys-org.description: Understanding how marine ecosystems respond to a warming ocean requires detailed records of past temperatures. An international research team led by Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) and the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry (MPIC) in Mainz has found a new way to reconstruct daily seawater temperatures over a four-month period.

phys-org.title: Marine heat waves pose hidden threat to human health, researchers warn
phys-org.description: The devastating impacts of marine heat waves extend far beyond dying coral reefs and declining fisheries, with new research warning that these extreme ocean-warming events pose a growing threat to human physical and mental health.

phys-org.title: Malaysian farmers, environmental groups call for rejection of GMO rice trial
phys-org.description: A coalition of farmers, consumer associations and environmental groups is urging Malaysia's National Biosafety Board to reject a proposed field trial of genetically modified rice, warning Tuesday the project could pose risks to food safety, the environment and farmers.

phys-org.title: Fungal chitin offers new route to tougher hydrogels for medical devices and soft robots
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Department of Energy's (DOE) Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and the University of Tennessee (UT), Knoxville, have made an advance by using a natural substance from fungi called chitin to create hydrogels that are significantly stronger and tougher. This new material could lead to safer medical devices, longer-lasting coatings and other innovations that improve everyday technology and health care.

phys-org.title: Consistency-based rewards could build lasting cooperation better than punishing free-riders
phys-org.description: A vaccine only protects a whole community if enough people get it, including those who would stay safe anyway once their neighbors are covered. The same tension runs through climate action and social movements: The shared payoff arrives only when enough people pitch in.

phys-org.title: Three energy-loss routes may explain Tarantula Nebula's X-ray shortfall
phys-org.description: Like a collage made of layered sheets of colored cellophane, a vibrant new image layers observations of a famous star-forming nebula from NASA's space telescopes. The resulting cosmic "craft" reveals new details about the star-forming region known as 30 Doradus, or the Tarantula Nebula.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Return of the Power Trust
proj-syn.description: A century ago, the US power industry was dominated by sprawling, heavily indebted holding companies until their collapse forced the federal government to break them up. Now, the pattern is repeating, with mega-mergers and buyouts advancing a debt-heavy business model at the expense of households and communities.

proj-syn.title: Morocco’s Bet on Targeted AI
proj-syn.description: Rather than join the global race for computing power, Morocco has focused on building sovereignty over its data, talent, and uses of AI, because technological power will be measured by usefulness, not by domination. This strategy calls for the country to embrace innovation without ceding its identity to foreign models.

proj-syn.title: Dude, Where’s My Recession?
proj-syn.description: Despite a series of major negative shocks, some of them unprecedented, the US economy continues to grow in line with its estimated long-run potential. Yet given obvious and mounting risks, from debt-financed speculation to geopolitical tensions, the appearance of resilience should not be confused with the real thing.

proj-syn.title: The Token Economy Requires Collective Data Governance
proj-syn.description: Millions of people continuously generate the raw material on which AI is trained, yet almost none shares in the wealth it creates. This underscores the need for data cooperatives representing internet users, creators, and other rights holders to negotiate access to the content being fed to large language models.

proj-syn.title: Excess Savings Are Driving the New China Shock
proj-syn.description: The current China shock combines continued supply upgrading with an absorption problem: the decline in property and related investment has reduced domestic demand, but national saving remains very high. The result is a larger savings-investment surplus that spills into net exports.

proj-syn.title: The World Economy Is Swerving, and the Destination Is Unknown
proj-syn.description: The days of unfettered globalization, multilateral rule of law, commonly accepted limits on economic statecraft, and widely shared macroeconomic objectives are now long gone. A perpetual, directionless transition is our new reality, and corporate executives, investors, and policymakers must adapt accordingly.

proj-syn.title: Is China Really a Beggar-thy-Neighbor Power?
proj-syn.description: When major economies are running at near full capacity, it is not clear that trade deficits should be a cause for concern, since they represent a transfer of purchasing power from surplus countries. Under the current circumstances, then, China’s widely criticized surpluses might as well be called enrich-thy-neighbor.

proj-syn.title: No Escape from the Russian Terror Playbook
proj-syn.description: When Vladimir Putin revives Stalin-era repression tactics, he does not do so in service of some lofty ideology or grand project. Rather, he and his security apparatus are seeking to safeguard their own power indefinitely—and, as Russians well know, they will stop at nothing to succeed.

proj-syn.title: The Extractive Trap Has a Green Exit
proj-syn.description: For resource-rich developing countries, decades of resource extraction have produced income concentration, economic dependency, external vulnerabilities, and the weakening of other productive sectors. Achieving broad-based prosperity requires a new approach, one which leverages South-South cooperation to build green industries.

proj-syn.title: The Last Trump Election
proj-syn.description: No matter what US President Donald Trump says or does in response to the results of this November’s midterms, he will have faced his final popular vote. There will be further damage done to public confidence in American democratic institutions, but the institutions themselves will hold.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.
